notes: Matched case-control study (Le 1998); ID the matched sets, a case and its controls matched on age, race and county. Faraway's ELM, as UCLA's Biostat 200C slides run it, leaves out the seven Down-syndrome cases and their controls (every Down-syndrome child is a case), fits clogit(disease ~ Sex + Mray + Fray + CnRay + strata(ID)), then drops Sex, Mray and CnRay's quadratic and cubic contrasts: clogit(disease ~ Fray + unclass(CnRay) + strata(ID)). Rendered as a random-intercept logistic on ID for its grouping (amlxray ruling, m3#23); the Down-syndrome subset stays in notes. age is a matching variable, constant within a set; CnRay is ordered, entered as its score. Outside check: the final model replaces the first fit's eight covariates.

Wedderburn (1974) quasi-binomial proportion example (also McCullagh & Nelder). 10 barley varieties at 9 sites, one obs per cell; blotch is a proportion with no trials column, filed continuous. Documented fit is fixed-effects on site and variety; rendered as random intercept on site (location block) per the Census blocking rule. Retained site assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of sites; this remains unverified. Outside check: stands.

notes: NONLINEAR: Brillinger and Preisler (1984, Bulletin of the Seismological Society of America 74, 1441), as GPT cites them, model accel^(1/3) in mag and log(dist^2 + h^2) with h estimated and random earthquake effects; the paper was not read here (the publisher blocks scripts). The R help's log-log display is a coplot, not a fit. Documented model is lm(DurationOfPrefix ~ Frequency + SpeechRate) (Pluymaekers, Ernestus and Baayen 2005) after the help's Frequency = log(Frequency + 1), rendered as its random-effects version on the repeated grouping Speaker (131 speakers over 428 rows). Documented model is lm(DurationOfPrefix ~ (YearOfBirth + SpeechRate) * Frequency) (Pluymaekers et al. 2005), rendered as its random-effects version on the repeated grouping Speaker (63 speakers over 102 rows, most with one); the help also fits fixed-effects models for PlosivePresent (model 2) and DurationPrefixNasal (model 3). Frequency is already logarithmic. Outside check: stands.

The help fits lrm(PlosivePresent ~ SpeechRate + YearOfBirth) (rms), whether the /t/ of ont- is present (Pluymaekers et al. 2005), rendered with a random intercept on the repeated grouping Speaker. Outside check: filed from the help.

The help fits lm(DurationPrefixNasal ~ PlosivePresent + Frequency + YearOfBirth), the duration of the /n/ (Pluymaekers et al. 2005), then refits it without four outliers, a subset fit; rendered with a random intercept on the repeated grouping Speaker. Outside check: filed from the help.

[XT] xtfrontier panel stochastic-frontier production function: xtfrontier lnwidgets lnmachines lnworkers, ti, whose time-invariant inefficiency u_i is truncated-normal N+(mu, sigma_u^2) with mu estimated, entering as -u_i. machines/workers are the raw untransformed inputs; t is the time index. The inefficiency is rendered as a Gaussian random intercept on id (frontier ruling, m3#24), published as amlxray's matched sets are. Outside check: the manual read, where the reading recalled a half-normal term.

MixedModels.jl benchmark dataset (docs/src/benchmarks.md fits d3:1+U+(1|G)+(1|H)+(1|I) and the random-slope variant); no source states its origin or simulation, so it stays by the #22 rule (decided 2026-10-07, #24, after a search of the MixedModels.jl repository and docs). 130418 rows; g is the composite of h (172 coded ids, 10001-style) and i (34 levels), u an integer 0-29, y an integer -50..50 symmetric about 0. Identity unknown; the agent had excluded it as simulated on structure alone. Outside check: stands; the slope variant y ~ 1 + u + (1 + u|g) + (1 + u|h) + (1 + u|i), the only d3 model of test/modelcache.jl, shares the response and grouping and files no row.

Read headache.txt (two-period three-treatment crossover for tension headache; Laird, Skinner & Kenward 1992). y = average pain relief over two headaches per period; trt is a string factor (A/B/P), six sequences. No R, SAS or Stata code of Fitzmaurice, Laird and Ware's book fits it. id is unique across the 14 centers (423 subjects), so center:id is id; center is a multi-centre cluster kept per the #24 repeating-cluster rule though the crossover model uses subject only; 'sequence' left to columns.csv. Model inferred, low. Outside check: no published model.

formula: logp ~ time + group + group:time + group:I((time - 7) * (time > 7)) + (time | id) + a penalized linear spline in time with knots at -7 to 14, its 22 coefficients iid random
notes: PdG hormone profiles over the menstrual cycle (Brumback & Rice 1998): 51 cycles from 51 women (22 conceptive, 29 non-conceptive); id = woman/cycle, logp = log PdG, group = conceptive vs not. The R code of Fitzmaurice, Laird and Ware (2011, sec. 19.5) fits the semiparametric model as a mixed model: lme(logp ~ time + group + group.time + group.bf15, random = list(Const = pdIdent(~ -1 + bf1 + ... + bf22), id = pdSymm(~time))), bf_k the truncated lines at knots -7 to 14 with one common variance, group.bf15 the group's hinge at day 7. The hinge and the spline stay in the formula only. Outside check: the book's model replaces the random-slope approximation.

Read ecg.txt (two-period crossover, cerebrovascular deficiency, ECG abnormality side-effect; Jones & Kenward 1989). y binary, 67 patients x 2 periods; id = subject, seq = treatment sequence (left in columns.csv). The R code of Fitzmaurice, Laird and Ware (2011, sec. 16.5) fits glmer(y ~ trt + period + (1 | id), family = binomial, nAGQ = 75) beside a marginal GEE. Outside check: stands, the book's code read.

formula: NoDisperse ~ Species + Male + ClanSize + AllKin + (1 | Year)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: NoDisperse (1 = did not disperse within 12 months of weaning) is the natal-dispersal outcome Hoogland.Rd describes, against the kin present (Hoogland 2013, Science 339). Grouped by Year (30 years from 1976). Species codes three prairie dogs (black-tailed, Gunnison's, Utah), a categorical design factor. AllKin is Mother + Sisters + Bros on all 1,720 rows with kin recorded, so the three parts are left out. Outside check: the kin parts dropped for their sum, Species categorical.

formula: cbind(num_amtl, sockets - num_amtl) ~ age + tooth_class + prob_male + genus + (1 | specimen)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: ante-mortem tooth loss, num_amtl teeth lost of sockets per specimen and tooth class (Anterior/Posterior/Premolar), 484 specimens over 1,450 rows. AMTL.Rd cites Gilmore (2013, American Journal of Physical Anthropology), who compares tooth loss in four genera (Homo, Pan, Papio, Pongo) by age and sex; rendered as a binomial with a random intercept per specimen. stdev_age (the age's uncertainty) and pop ignored. Outside check: genus added as a covariate.

formula: kg.meat ~ poly(age, 3, raw = TRUE) + hours + date + (poly(age, 3, raw = TRUE) | id) + (1 | year:month:day), as a hurdle: a Bernoulli part for zero returns and a Gamma part for positive ones with these terms each, the hunter effects correlated across parts with a hunter dispersion effect, date the Julian day of year, month and day
notes: Hunting returns of individual Ache men, 1981 to 2007 (Achehunting.Rd; Hill and Kintigh 2009). McElreath and Koster (2014, Human Nature 25) fit model Vary_9hDv to these trips (model_fitting_code.R; the paper was not read here, the publisher blocks scripts): a hurdle with a Bernoulli part for zero returns and a Gamma part for positive ones, each with a cubic in standardized age, hours and the Julian date, nine correlated hunter effects (both cubics and a dispersion) and a correlated pair of day effects. The code fixes two day codes (3157 to 31, -74 to 15), drops the six trips without a date and imputes hours where datatype says they are unknown (84% of rows). The cubic is in the formula only. McElreath's 2022 course (week 9) fits nonlinear Bernoulli and lognormal models of the same column by hunter (m2, m3, m4), which file no row. Outside check: the paper's model replaces the reading's linear proposal.

formula: nonlinear strength-growth Poisson rate of nuts_opened in seconds and age/max(age), phi varying by chimpanzee
notes: NONLINEAR: nuts_opened ~ Poisson(lambda), lambda = seconds * phi * (1 - exp(-k * age/max(age)))^theta (McElreath 2020, Statistical Rethinking, m16.4, R code 16.11), the opening rate rising with strength as a chimpanzee grows; exercise 16H2 asks for phi or k varying by chimpanzee (22 chimpanzees, 84 sessions). Panda_nuts.Rd cites Boesch et al. (2019). sex and hammer are columns no fit takes. Outside check: the book's model replaces the reading's additive count model.
